# OBS005 `specific-intrinsic-name`

<Badge type="warning" text="warning" /> <Badge type="tip" text="enabled by default" />

A specific intrinsic name (`dsqrt`, `dabs`, `amax1`, `float` ...) instead of the generic one.

## Why

Specific names fix the argument kind (`dsqrt` only accepts double precision), so changing the kind
of a variable breaks or silently converts the call. The generic names (`sqrt`, `abs`, `max`,
`real`) work for every kind. Specific names are obsolescent since Fortran 2018.

## Reported

```fortran
y = dsqrt(x) + float(n)
```

## Preferred

```fortran
y = sqrt(x) + real(n, kind(x))
```

## Suppressing

For one occurrence, with the reason on the same line (or alone on the line before the statement):

```fortran
! fobis: ignore[OBS005] <why this occurrence is fine>
```

For the whole project, `ignore = OBS005` in the fobos [`[lint]` section](/cookbook/analysis#choose-the-rules).
